messages:
incident-bot: SEV:high Capacity-tier routing anomalies detected for tenant shard group 'eu-ssd-1' — elevated fallback rate from DEDICATED -> HOSTED (spillover) and multiple 5xxs. Alert window start 2165702468
john: paging oncall, I'm seeing 502/503 spikes and a lot of fallback logs pointing to policy eval picking hosted variants incorrectly
maria: on it, grabbing traces. John, can you paste the policy id from the logs?
john: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-06T08:12:12Z] tenant=acme-corp shard=eu-ssd-1 policy=policy::capacity-tier-v2 eval=[tier_preference: [hosted, dedicated], fallback_models: [gpt-small-quant, gpt-medium-qa]] chosen=hosted/gpt-small-quant
```
maria: oh no — tier_preference shows hosted before dedicated for that policy. That shouldn't be the case for enterprise shards.
dinesh: I see the diff in the last policy rollout: the canary accidentally inverted the priority for tenants matching `^acme-.*` when fallback_mode=allow-hosted. PR 4981 changed default ordering to `hosted,dedicated` for a small set of internal tests and it leaked into production canary
eva: customer impact: acme-corp reporting high latencies and degraded generations over the last 10m. CS pinged.
anna-cs: acme's SRE says timeouts are causing partial failures in their webhook pipeline; they're seeing ~15% error rate. They've opened a support ticket.
tess-product: tagging product — this affected a single high-value tenant; we need mitigation and comms.
john: mitigation proposal: 1) revert policy change for policy::capacity-tier-v2 2) force route acme-corp to dedicated pool for active sessions 3) rollback any model-variant fallbacks to gpt-medium-qa
maria: agree. I'm applying a hotfix now to swap tier order back to `dedicated,hosted` for the acme regex and any shard-scoped policies. Running dry-run then apply.
deploy-bot: started deployment 2165702650: patch/policy-hotfix -> infra-config (canary 10% -> staging -> prod)
maria: applied patch to canary (10% of shards). Monitoring.
john: canary looks healthy, no more fallbacks in those shards. Moving to immediate full apply.
maria: full apply complete 2165702882. Rolling config change propagated to all eu shards. Please confirm metrics.
dinesh: metrics show fallback rate -> hosted dropped from 38% -> 2% within 90s. 503 rate down to baseline.
eva: acme-corp latency percentiles improving. CS confirmed partial mitigation message to customer.
anna-cs: acme got back to us: partial recovery, but they noted some incorrect model outputs during the 10m window (gpt-small-quant was lower quality). They want an RCA and remediation plan.
john: next steps: create temporary instrumentation to identify all tenants that were matched by the bad regex, export list, and run a replay check for any requests that experienced hosted fallbacks. We should also tag affected sessions for later compensation.
maria: running query now: `select tenant, count(*) as fallbacks from requests where policy='capacity-tier-v2' and chosen='hosted' and ts between 2165702400 and 2165703000 group by tenant order by fallbacks desc limit 200;`

maria: results: acme-corp (870 fallbacks), beta-inc (34), internal-test (12), partner-x (6)

john: acme is clearly the one. Dinesh, let's roll back the PR that introduced the invert and add an automated test for policy ordering.
dinesh: on it. PR 4981 revert in progress. Adding unit+integration test to assert `tier_preference` stable ordering for tenant-scoped policies.

deploy-bot: started deployment 2165703250: revert/pr-4981 -> infra-config

john: handoff — I'm going offline in 30m. Maria, can you take incident lead for postmortem and comms? I'll keep available for pager follow-ups.
maria: taking lead. I'll own investigation, RCA, and customer comms draft. Opening SEV ticket and postmortem doc.
maria: SEV ticket created: SEV-2026-013

anna-cs: sending customer note now: high-level summary + ETA for RCA. Will mention compensation offer for degraded outputs.
teams-notify-bot: notified #executive-alerts with short incident summary.

maria: quick root cause summary: a canary change in policy generation accidentally inverted capacity tier order for tenant-scoped regex due to a defaults merge bug. This caused service to prefer hosted variants for certain enterprise tenants leading to increased latency and lower-quality model fallbacks. No data exfiltration.

maria: immediate remediation: reverted policy, forced session routing to dedicated for affected tenants, rolled back PR 4981, added monitoring alert for tier-preference drift

dinesh: long-term fix items: 1) stricter CI for policy generator, 2) release gating for canary promos that touch tenant-scoped configs, 3) post-deploy verification job to assert tenant isolation semantics

john: FYI the number: incident window ~ 08:12:12 -> 08:20:00 UTC (roughly 8 minutes). Affected tenant count: 4 (1 high-impact). Peak affected requests ~ 38% fallbacks for acme during peak.
eva: severity classification: SEV-2 due to single-customer degradation and partial platform degradation. Product and CS concur.

maria: doc checklist for postmortem:
- timeline + artifacts (logs, diffs)
- rollback timeline and commands
- affected tenant list
- customer comms draft
- action items + owners

maria: assigning owners: dinesh -> policy-ci tests, john -> verification job, anna-cs -> customer follow-up, eva -> alert tuning, tess-product -> business comms

john: quick note for oncall handoff: maria will be primary POC. I'm setting my status to OOO but will check if page escalates.
maria: thanks — taking it. I'll schedule a 1hr follow-up sync with eng, product, and CS at 09:00 UTC and drop the postmortem link here when ready.

deploy-bot: deployment 2165703250 completed successfully.

maria: posting initial postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/SEV-2026-013 (draft)

anna-cs: sent follow-up to acme: apology, summary of mitigation, offer to re-run 870 affected requests offline with corrected routing and upgraded model variant free of charge. Waiting for their reply.

maria: closing incident channel for active mitigation. Will update here after RCA finalized. Thanks all for quick action :tada:

john: thanks team, signing off.
